text:
Sam P: Heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate for /v1/chat/generate on redwood-13b-quant. Dashboard shows 72% -> 38% over the last 2h for global traffic. looks like token-saved tanked too.
Maya R: yikes. do you have the grafana link? any customer slice obvious? :eyes:
Sam P: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/prefix-hit?panelId=7 — main spike centered at 2026-03-18T10:12 UTC. top affected customers: acme, bluewave, labco.
Derek (eng-runtime): saw same. also correlates with a deploy at ~09:50 that touched the chat prompt templating code. low-level KV hits drop but backend latency unchanged.
Anika K: pulling 1k sampled requests from acme. a lot of tiny prefix variations: added session metadata and a new `user_intent` slot in the prompt. looks like keying is sensitive to that.
Leo: was there a normalization change in the keying function? we switched to `json.dumps` ordering recently for structured slots, maybe that made prefixes unique.
Sam P: good point — I checked commit history: PR #4242 replaced canonicalize_prefix with a new `compact_json` path that keeps keys in insertion order. that would break previous deduping.
perf-bot: regression-alert: prefix-hit-drop-4802 triggered (drop 34% on /v1/chat/generate)
Maya R: OK that explains divergence. two quick asks: 1) can we add a temporary grafana panel showing hit-rate by prefix-hash (top 50) so we can see cardinality explosion? 2) make an alert on token-saved % delta per-customer.
Derek (eng-runtime): will do panel. query I'll use: `sum by(prefix_hash)(hits) / sum by(prefix_hash)(requests)` + moving_avg(5m). also we should emit cardinality metric: `prefix_cardinality{route="/chat/generate"}` per-customer.
Anika K: posting a small sample of request prefixes (sanitized):
```
{"session_id":"s-123","user_intent":"order_status","items":[]}
{"session_id":"s-124","user_intent":"order_status","items":[]}
{"session_id":"s-125","user_intent":"support","items":[]}
```
These differ only by session_id which we should strip from cache key.
Leo: agree — cache key should only include stable context: model, route, canonicalized prompt tokens, and explicit slots annotated as cache-relevant. session_id must be excluded.
Sam P: action plan proposal: revert to previous canonicalize_prefix temporarily for 2h canary; add a normalization step that strips transient fields; add grafana cardinality panel + per-customer token-saved alert.
Derek (eng-runtime): I'll patch canary and add panel. will also ship a histogram of prefix length and unique-hash count per-customer.
Maya R: also add a light-weight sampling recorder (1/100 requests) that logs the raw prefix -> cache_key mapping to S3 for offline audit.
Anika K: will run quick eval to estimate token-saved delta if we roll back — I expect regained ~30-35% tokens for acme slice.
perf-bot: deploy-canary started for eng-runtime/canonicalize-revert @canary-3
Leo: long-term we should enforce a schema for prompt slots and surface slot-level cache annotations in the console so product teams don't accidentally add high-cardinality slots.
Sam P: agreed. for now owners: Derek -> canary + panels; Maya -> alerts + sampling; Anika -> sample analysis & estimate; Leo -> design for slot-schema. target: full rollback or schema fix by EOD.
Maya R: tagging #product and #devex so they can review slot annotations. @product please FYI. :bell:
Derek (eng-runtime): will post results in this thread once canary has run 15m.
Sam P: thanks all. keeping an eye on customer Slack channels and PS. :thumbsup:
